meta.title: Locus Atlas
meta.tagline: Review the guarantees, check the implementation, and use the result from ordinary Rust.

features.name: bool, and the eight machine integer types with the wrapping methods
Unit and tuples, with a later field able to mention an earlier one inside a proposition
Field access by name on a tuple with named fields
features.note: By design the names are binders; `.0` or `let` reads a field (tests/corpus/reject/field_of_a_tuple_by_name.lc)

features.name: Structs with proof fields
Enums, including recursive physical data through Box
A function of the logic named as evidence of its general claim
features.note: Replaces the math fn type. tests/corpus/accept/explicit_steps.lc

features.name: i32, u32 and the other machine widths
Int: unbounded, logic-only, reached with `as Int`
Library Nat, Seq, Maybe and finite maps; general Set API remains future
Model observations replace Ghost<T> and snapshot!(e)
features.note: Ghost and snapshot spellings produce tested migration diagnostics; tests/reconcile_logic.rs

features.name: Floats
features.note: Executable only; not usable in propositions.

features.name: Arrays, parameter slices, Vec and Box; Arc and strings remain future
Recursive logical data and physical recursion through Box
Generics, Logical derive, Model impls and logical closures; general traits and runtime closures remain future
dyn
let, blocks, shadowing
if and else, with a fact for each branch
Comparisons, &&, || and ! with separate bool/Bool/Prop meanings
match on an enum, with `Enum::Variant(names)`, `Enum::Variant { fields, .. }`, and `_` arms
Literal, struct, and nested patterns; let with a constructor pattern
Rust's `loop` with `break value`, `while`, and `continue`, over `let mut`
`for` over a range of any integer type, exclusive or inclusive, with `break`
let mut and assignment, whole and by a field path
Arithmetic operators + - * / % with Rust's behavior; in a proposition only total operations
while, for over iterators, if let
features.note: `while` is built; `for` over an iterator and `while let` are refused (tests/corpus/reject/loops_not_yet.lc); `if let` is a syntax error

features.name: Prelude Option and Result; ? and let else remain future
features.note: tests/reconcile_generics.rs; runtime instances emit specialized enums, not std::option::Option ABI

features.name: panic!, assert!, unreachable!, todo!, debug_assert! as built-in forms
Loops that promise to terminate
Prop, @P, prop!(F), connectives; quantifier keywords lower to library propositions
Named proposition arms with witness parameters and one explicit @ evidence slot
`_` and `prove!` filled by fixed tiers: stored, exact, computed, evaluation, arithmetic
A failed `_` reports the claim, the claim after computing, the facts, and a counterexample
Evidence must match the claim exactly after computing
Proof constructors, match on evidence, `match h {}` on evidence of false
rewrite!, unfold!, fold!
Applying evidence of a forall or an implication; a function of the logic named as evidence
162 lemmas about Int and every machine type, callable by name
const
Exists construction and proof-scoped witness elimination
features.note: tests/reconcile_quantifier_library.rs; arbitrary witness extraction is rejected

features.name: Tracked evidence: `let mut` evidence invalidated by assignment, refreshed explicitly, carried by loops
A decision procedure for arithmetic that produces certificates
Logical function values and explicit congruence; general congruence closure remains future
Checked lemma libraries written in Locus
Ordinary fn may diverge; only logic fn enters propositions
features.note: tests/reconcile_logic.rs; promises do not change function mode

features.name: Promises: terminates, no_panic, no_alloc, no_io
Logical functions are pure, total and return Logical values
features.note: tests/reconcile_logic.rs; runtime arguments are observed without moving data

features.name: Structural logical recursion and explicit Int descent through recurse!
Mutually recursive logical enum groups; mutually recursive functions remain future
& and &mut as parameters; old!(x); impl blocks and self
Shared references in locals, records and results, with lifetimes
features.note: tests/reconcile_shared.rs; tier excludes reference leaves in owned heap payloads and stored mutable references

features.name: Moves, types that are not Copy, Clone
&mut in locals, returned, or in structs
features.note: Not planned; the cost of each is recorded in Mutation and references.

features.name: Interior mutability, unsafe, async, Drop
Kernel gates K1 to K6
features.note: Equality, products, functions, cases and declared propositions, Int and the machine models, range iteration; the internal Nat was removed at R4

features.name: Closed evaluation, and the linear arithmetic rule
features.note: Replaces the proof by 256 cases. tests/kernel_evaluation.rs, tests/kernel_linear.rs

features.name: Typed tree, lowering, the check IR and its checker
Single Erased marker, effect-preserving erasure and unused-marker cleanup
Differential testing of the two branches, and random programs three ways
Parser for the core grammar: every Rust keyword reserved, Rust's precedence, total by a step and a depth bound
Elaborator: names, ordering of declarations, types, holes
Command line: check, run, rust, build, with --holes, --stats, --locked
Proofs file of found proofs, so that checking again does not search again; --locked
Checked data induction, recursive predicates and monomorphic generic instances
locus audit; formal erasure theorem and independent checker export remain future
features.note: tests/audit.rs; Process P10 documents the unmechanized calculus

features.name: Generated interfaces that protect what was proven; pub(crate)
Header and implementation split
features.note: The header must elaborate on its own.

features.name: Modules and use, packages, features, tests
features.note: Rust's own mod, use, and pub.

features.name: Reason-bearing trusted Rust collection declarations; general foreign linking remains future
features.note: tests/trusted.rs; Vec len/get/push registry checks physical signature shape

features.name: A cargo and build.rs driver; the locus! on-ramp
features.note: Locus source tokenizes as Rust so that the macro stays possible.

features.name: Diagnostics as JSON; an LSP server; a reference and example corpus for models
Verified sequence and collection models; broad standard library remains future
prove!(P): state a claim where it stands; the fact stays in scope and the value is evidence
Built-in forms spelled with !, and no user-defined macros
features.note: matches! and vec! wait for their types (tests/corpus/reject/unknown_form.lc)

features.name: rewrite!, fold! and unfold! construct checked transport/definition proofs
features.note: tests/reconcile_props.rs; tests/reconcile_models.rs; kernel derive helpers remain untrusted

features.name: prop!(P) for a proposition and @P for evidence; brackets left to arrays
Values move; Copy and Clone only by derive; use after move is an error
The never type !
Enum variants with named fields
Type arguments on the types the language provides
features.note: Ghost<T> is the one such type (tests/corpus/accept/ghost_values.lc)

features.name: Integer literals typed as in Rust: the expected type, else i32; suffixes and other bases
usize and isize
Tuple structs, unit structs, newtypes; explicit discriminants
return
Rust's operator precedence, exactly
== and != on bool and every integer type
match with the power it has in Rust
features.note: Integers, bool, tuples; literal, range, and or-patterns; @ bindings; guards.

features.name: Constants checked in logical initialization; erased constants do not execute
Private by default, and pub
Every Rust keyword reserved
Paths of any length; separate type and value namespaces
features.note: Paths through modules wait for modules (tests/corpus/reject/module_paths_not_yet.lc). tests/corpus/accept/namespaces.lc

features.name: Doc comments and chosen attributes passed through to generated Rust
Int and the machine integer models in the kernel; an arithmetic procedure that produces evidence
Bit operators and shifts
features.note: After the core; they need a bit-level model.

features.name: Operators a programmer defines, through the operator traits
features.note: Integers, in code and in propositions. Arrives with traits; how such an operator states when it does not panic is open.
